o: Convert each "MM-DD" into a day-of-year number using cumulative month lengths for a non-leap year. The together-days are the intersection of two inclusive intervals: max(0, min(leaveA, leaveB) − max(arriveA, arriveB) + 1). Example 1: Alice [227,230], Bob [228,231] → intersection [228,230] = 3 days. Example 2: intervals [274,304] and [305,365] don't intersect → 0.
k: Map dates to integers so interval intersection becomes simple arithmetic.
Inclusive endpoints mean the intersection length is min(leaves) − max(arrives) + 1, clamped at 0.

a.n: Approach 1: Prefix day conversion + interval intersection
a.i: Precompute cumulative days per month, convert all four dates to day numbers, then apply the standard interval-overlap formula.
s: Return max(0, min(leaveAlice, leaveBob) − max(arriveAlice, arriveBob) + 1) on converted values.
a.t: O(1) — at most 12-month prefix computation and constant arithmetic.

w: This is a one-liner after date conversion; mention the clamp at 0 explicitly. Pitfalls: treating intervals as half-open (forgetting +1), and mishandling identical arrival/leave dates. Follow-up: support multiple people, or leap years (add Feb 29 conditionally).
